edges.description: Environmental acquisition introduces the dimorphic fungus into tissue where Hcd is detected as large thick-walled yeast cells.
Persistent Hcd yeasts elicit granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells containing fungal forms.
Persistent tissue infection can disseminate to at least two noncontiguous body sites in a substantial fraction of published cases.
Disseminated and HIV-associated Hcd infection can present with fever.
Granulomatous inflammation in skin produces cutaneous lesions.
Granulomatous infection of bone produces osteomyelitis.
Soil admixed with bat guano acts upstream of human Hcd acquisition, but the portal and exposure steps for African histoplasmosis are not yet settled.
Advanced HIV-associated immunosuppression weakens cellular control of Histoplasma infection and is observed in disseminated Hcd case reports.
